proves: None is answered, not raised. A splitter or expander that threw on a blank cell would push a try block into every caller reading a schema export.
An identifier that tokenises to nothing has no token that failed to resolve, so is_fully_known is true vacuously and the empty tokens tuple is what says nothing was expanded.
Blank input holds no letters and no digits, so there is nothing to split.
Separators-only input yields no tokens rather than three empty ones.
Runs of separators collapse, so a doubled underscore reads exactly like a single one and contributes no empty token.
A leading or trailing separator contributes nothing either.
Lower-case input resolves identically and raw records the casing that was written, so the audit record shows the token as the schema actually spelled it.
Dots, hyphens, slashes and spaces all separate, and a run of several of them collapses to one boundary.
Letter/digit boundaries split in both directions. ADDRESS spelled out is not the governed ADDR and is honestly reported unknown, which is the behaviour that makes the miss fixable.
A digit before a letter is a boundary too, and the digit token is not joined to what follows because no catalog row vouches for 7Code.
An empty GovernedDictionary is the supported spelling of no governed vocabulary, and it passes everything through. This is the shape the verbs point at when they refuse dictionary=None.

With nothing governed, the reverse direction upper-cases and stops. It does not clip either word to make it look like an abbreviation, and no class word is appended because the empty vocabulary does not govern one.
An empty name normalises to an empty name rather than stopping a batch.
Casing is corrected to UPPER_SNAKE, which is the only change a name of approved tokens needs.
normalize rebuilds a name from its tokens, so a name written without separators gains them. That is the same boundary judgement every other verb here makes about the string.
Every unapproved token the catalog names an approved form for is rewritten to it, and nothing else is touched. This is exactly the set of fixes is_compliant reported for the same name.

A token nothing knows is left exactly as it stands. An unknown rewritten to a guess is worse than an unknown reported as unknown, so normalize is not a promise of compliance - is_compliant still fails this name.
An empty name is reported as a finding rather than raised, so a batch of names being checked does not stop at the first blank row.
Separators-only input is the same case: there is no name to check.
An 87-character name built entirely from approved vocabulary is compliant under the default policy, because the default does not enforce a length ceiling at all.
The same name under strict_length fails, and name comes back in full. The policy changes the verdict and nothing else - it may only ever raise a flag.

input.arg: Customer Account Primary Owner Party Identifier

proves: The rendered name is 32 characters against a 30-character ceiling and comes back whole, with all six tokens and truncated false. enforce_name_length is not consulted by this direction at all, and no policy setting can make it drop a token.
